content: Rehmannia is a genus consisting of six species of flowering plants that belong to the order Lamiales and are native to China. Historically, this genus was classified under the family Scrophulariaceae or Gesneriaceae in older taxonomic systems. However, it does not appear to fit within the broader clades of Lamiales, nor does it align with the family Phrymaceae, where many former Scrophulariaceae species have been reclassified. Rehmannia is sometimes referred to as Chinese Foxglove due to its superficial resemblance to the genus Digitalis. The plants in this genus are perennial herbs characterized by their large, showy flowers. They are cultivated as ornamental garden plants in Europe and North America and have significant medicinal applications in Asia. In traditional Chinese medicine, Rehmannia is known as dì huáng (地黄) or gān dì huáng (干地黄). One species, Rehmannia glutinosa, is widely used as a medicinal herb to treat various conditions, including anemia, dizziness, and constipation. The plant contains essential vitamins such as A, B, C, and D, along with other beneficial compounds. Interestingly, the name Rehmannia has also been assigned to a genus of Jurassic ammonites, which belong to the family Reineckeiidae.
